blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Deep research, or any use of large language models (LLMs) to read a large document collection and produce insights, requires synthesizing information from different sources. In this work, we find that LLMs produce long-form research reports that read as confident syntheses but which fail to accurately reflect the underlying documents. We call this failure smoothing. In collapsing diverse and potentially conflicting sources into a single narrative, the model discards the evidential "jaggedness" of its corpus and asserts conclusions more decisive than the citations can support. We introduce a claim level scoring pipeline, SmoothScore, to quantify this effect. Our pipeline extracts key conclusive claims from model generated reports, then finds evidence relevant to each claim and clusters that evidence along high level aspects. Finally, each claim is scored with respect to the evidence to quantify the degree of smoothing done by the agent. Across 7 systems and 4 datasets, we find that agents consistently produce stronger claims than warranted.
blocks.zh: 深入研究,或任何使用大型语言模型(LLMs)来读取大型文件集并产生见解,都需要从不同来源合成信息. 在这项工作中,我们发现LLMS产生长式的调查报告,读作自信的综述,但未能准确反映基本文件. 我们称之为故障平滑。 模型将各种可能相互冲突的来源合并成单一的叙述,从而抛弃了其主体证据的"标记",并断言结论比引用证据更具有决定性。 我们采用了一个索赔等级评分的管道,平滑分数,以量化这种影响。 我们的管道从模型生成的报告中取出关键的结论性索赔,然后找到与每项索赔有关的证据,并找出与高级别方面有关的证据。 最后,每项索赔的得分与确定代理人平滑程度的证据有关。 在整个7个系统和4个数据集中,我们发现,代理人不断提出比正当要求更强烈的要求。

blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Figure 1: When synthesizing over many documents, agents can present a claim as well supported when the evidence is actually more mixed. SmoothScore flags these smoothed-over claims and quantifies the degree of smoothing.
blocks.zh: 图1:当对许多文件进行综合时,当证据实际上比较混杂时,代理人可以提出索赔,也可以提出证明。 平滑的分数标记这些平滑的主张,并量化平滑的程度.

blocks.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are often deployed within systems that read across many sources of information and return long-form reports with citations ( Shao et al., 2026 ; Xie et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026b ; Nakano et al., 2021 ) . These systems, either general-purpose agents paired with Internet access or special-purpose “deep research” agents, retrieve large volumes of documents and analyze and synthesize this information into coherent reports ( Du et al., 2026 ; Onweller et al., 2026 ) . The skills required to do this go beyond simple multi-document summarization ( Fabbri et al., 2019 ) : agents must weigh evidence, integrate conflicting findings, and determine what the evidence warrants ( Narayanan Venkit et al., 2026 ; Rasheed et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ) . The resulting reports are typically fluent, well-organized, and densely cited, which makes them read as confident, authoritative syntheses. As a result, users increasingly treat these outputs as substitutes for reading the underlying literature, even when the synthesis misrepresents or overstates what the cited sources actually support ( Li and Aral, 2025 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 大语言模型(LLMS)经常部署在跨越许多信息来源的系统中,并用引文返回长式报告(Shao等人,2026年;Xie等人,2026年;Li等人,2026年b;Nakano等人,2021年). 这些系统或与互联网接入或特殊用途“深入研究”代理配合的通用代理,可检索大量文件,并分析这些资料并将其综合成一致的报告(Du等人,2026年;Onweller等人,2026年)。 这样做所需的技能超越了简单的多文件归纳(Fabbri等人,2019年):特工必须权衡证据,综合相互矛盾的调查结果,并确定证据理由(Narayanan Venkit等人,2026年;Rasheed等人,2026年;Zhu等人,2026年)。 由此产生的报告通常流利、组织良好和引用频繁,因此,它们被看作自信、权威的综合。 因此,用户越来越多地将这些产出作为阅读基本文献的替代物,即使合成曲解或过多地表述了引用来源实际支持的内容(Li and Arail,2025;Huang等人,2026).

blocks.en: In this work, we study the prevalence of smoothing in LLM generated reports. We define smoothing as the tendency of LLMs to synthesize claims that are more decisive than supported by the documents they cite. Such claims may, for example, fail to portray mixed evidence or overclaim a result to hold in all circumstances when it has only been shown more narrowly. By contrast, a faithful claim should hedge when the evidence is mixed and narrow its scope when the support is narrow.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们研究了LLM中平滑现象的普遍程度,由此产生了报告. 我们把平滑定义为LLMs将比它们所引用的文件支持的更具决定性的主张综合起来的倾向. 例如,这种索赔可能无法描述混杂的证据,或者在只有更狭义地说明的情况下,在一切情况下都存在过这种结果。 相比之下,在证据混杂时,忠实债权应当套期,在支持范围狭窄时缩小其范围.

blocks.en: To identify instances of this behavior, we propose SmoothScore , a framework for measuring whether the claims in a synthesized report are calibrated to the cited documents. As shown in Figure 1 , we find that an agent’s report can present a claim as well supported by some of its citations, even though other retrieved evidence shows the claim only holds under certain conditions. The bulk of prior work on claim verification and long-form factuality ( Min et al., 2023 ; Song et al., 2024 ; Tang et al., 2024 ) can check whether individual claims are supported by their cited evidence, but breaks down for synthesized claims: these systems usually return binary judgments at the claim or subclaim level, but do not handle calibration and scoping across a large body of potentially conflicting evidence.
blocks.zh: 为了查明这种行为的事例,我们提议采用SmoothScore(SmoothScore)这一框架,用以衡量一份综合报告中的说法是否与所引用的文件相符。 如图1所示,我们发现,代理人的报告可以提出索赔,而且可以援引其中的一些证据作为佐证,尽管其他检索的证据表明,索赔只在某些条件下存在。 以前关于索赔核实和长形式事实性的大部分工作(Min等人,2023年;Song等人,2024年;Tang等人,2024年)可以核实个人索赔是否得到所引用证据的支持,但为综合索赔而分解:这些系统通常在索赔或次级索赔一级返回二进制判决,但不处理大量可能相互冲突的证据的校准和范围界定。

blocks.en:
To compute SmoothScore , we first decompose each report into its main conclusive claims and identify the documents the report cites. As shown in Figure 2 , for each claim, we run two agents over the report’s cited documents: (a) Support Agent : which surfaces evidence consistent with the claim, and (b) Skeptic Agent : which actively searches for evidence that qualifies, limits, or contradicts the claim. Evidence from both these passes are clustered into aspects reflecting different dimensions of the claim, such as viewpoint, strength of argument, and certainty ( Kargupta et al., 2025 ) .
Given the claim and its mapped aspect-evidence pairs, we score the claim’s calibration on a 1–5 scale, reflecting how well its stated strength and scope match the evidence collected across both passes.
blocks.zh:
为了计算平滑得分,我们首先将每份报告分解为其主要结论性索赔,并确定报告所引用的文件。 如图2所示,对每一项索赔,我们都要对报告所引述的文件进行两项调查:(a) 支助代理人:哪些证据与索赔相符;(b) 怀疑代理人:哪些证据可积极寻找符合、限制或与索赔相矛盾的证据。 这两段路段的证据被归纳为反映索赔不同层面的方面,例如观点、论据的力量和确定性(Kargupta等人,2025年)。
鉴于索赔及其标注的方面证据对等,我们按1至5个尺度对索赔的校准进行评分,以反映索赔所陈述的强度和范围与所收集的证据如何相符。

blocks.en: Across four benchmarks and seven systems, we find that smoothing is pervasive. On average, for each system at least 25% of generated claims received a SmoothScore ≥ 3 \geq 3 . For most systems over half of claims show at least material smoothing, and up to 35% of Gemini Deep Research’s claims show severe smoothing ( ≥ 4 \geq 4 ). We also find that limited interaction with the cited documents contributes to smoothing: Luna opens only 19% of the pages it cites, and actively engaging with the full documents can help reduce smoothing.
blocks.zh: 在四个基准和七个系统中,我们发现平滑是普遍的。 平均而言,每个系统至少25%的索赔收到平滑分数 3 \ geq 3。 对于大多数系统来说,超过一半的索赔要求至少显示材料的平滑,多达35%的双子座深层研究索赔要求显示严重平滑(QQ 4\geq 4 )。 我们还发现,与上述文件的有限互动有助于平滑: Luna只打开它引用的19%的页面,而积极接触完整的文件有助于降低平滑度.

blocks.en: Contributions Our main contributions are: (a) We introduce SmoothScore , a framework for measuring whether the claims in a synthesized report are calibrated to the strength and scope of their cited evidence, rather than merely supported by it and (b) we find this issue to be widespread across frontier systems on 4 different benchmarks.
blocks.zh: 捐款 我们的主要贡献是:(a) 我们采用 " 平稳得分 " ,这是衡量综合报告中的说法是否与其所引述证据的力度和范围相一致的框架,而不只是得到其支持;(b) 我们发现这一问题在四个不同基准的前沿系统中普遍存在。

blocks.en: We call a claim smoothed if it satisfies three criteria:(1) it reflects a conclusion drawn from aggregated evidence; (2) some of the evidence supports at least part of the conclusion; and (3) the conclusion as a whole is stronger or broader than the body of the evidence warrants.
blocks.zh: 如果索赔符合以下三项标准,则我们称索赔得到理顺:(1) 索赔反映了从综合证据中得出的结论;(2) 一些证据至少支持部分结论;(3) 整个结论比证据证明书更有力或更广泛。

blocks.en: This goal is closely related to hallucination detection ( Zha et al., 2023 ; Min et al., 2023 ; Tang et al., 2024 ) ; we view it as a special case of hallucination detection. However, typical methods for hallucination detection assume binary factuality judgments. Past work has looked at more nuanced judgments for narrative summarization ( Subbiah et al., 2025 ) and opinion summarization ( Bhaskar et al., 2023 ) , but these methods are designed for simpler settings and do not handle the complexity of smoothing in deep research systems.
blocks.zh: 这个目标与幻觉检测密切相关(Zha等人,2023年;Min等人,2023年;Tang等人,2024年);我们把它视为幻觉检测的特例. 然而,典型的幻觉检测方法假设二元事实判断. 过去的工作研究了叙述性总结(Subbiah等人,2025年)和意见性总结(Bhaskar等人,2023年)的更细微的判断,但这些方法是为更简单的环境设计的,无法处理深层研究系统中平滑的复杂性.

blocks.en:
Evaluating whether a claim is smoothed requires more than checking whether a report’s statements are supported by individual citations. For instance, in Figure 2 , the extracted claim ‘discrete image-token modeling
appears more promising than a Stable-Diffusion-centered architecture’ is a conclusion made by the deep research system (satisfying condition (1) above). It is supported by the cited documents, D 1 D_{1} Emu3 paper ( Wang et al., 2024 ) ) and D 3 D_{3} (the Show-o paper ( Xie et al., 2025 ) ) (satisfying condition (2)). However, we find that the same sources along with other documents, namely D 2 D_{2} (the Transfusion paper ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) ), also contains results that show that the statement is only true under certain conditions present counter evidence (satisfying condition (3)).
Therefore, smoothing can occur even when a claim appears supported, and methods producing binary judgments from small evidence sets cannot comprehensively capture the distribution to identify it.

评估索赔是否平稳,需要的不仅仅是检查报告的陈述是否附有个别引文。 例如,在图2中,所提取的索赔`分散的图像脚印模型'

blocks.en: We propose SmoothScore as a way of measuring the degree of smoothing a conclusion shows. Figure 2 outlines the pipeline. At a high level, first, we extract such claims from a generated report that represent the key takeaways, then find evidence that supports and refutes those claims. However, it is not straightforward to combine this evidence into a final score: counting supporting documents vs. refuting documents does not account for the nuances of how a claim is supported or refuted.
blocks.zh: 我们提议平滑评分作为衡量平滑结论显示程度的方法。 图2概述了管道。 首先,在高级别上,我们从一份代表主要外卖的报告中提取这种主张,然后找到支持和反驳这些主张的证据。 然而,将这种证据合并为最后分数并非直截了当的:计算证明文件与反驳文件并不说明如何支持或反驳索赔的细微差别。

blocks.en: Instead, for the claim c c in the report y y and evidence from a cited document d ∈ D d\in D , we identify a set of dimensions A ⁡ ( c , d ) = { a 1 , … , a k } A(c,d)=\{a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}\} that we call aspects , following ( Kargupta et al., 2025 ) . These aspects are consolidated across documents, to capture fine-grained ways in which a claim might be refuted. For instance, in Figure 2 , step 3, we are able to find ‘performance and efficiency of tokens vs diffusion models’ , under which we see some evidence state that ‘tokens match or beat diffusion’ but we also see evidence for ‘diffusion or hybrid set ups are competitive’ . As aspects are discovered per claim and tailored to the claim and its evidence, we use them to score claim against the aspect-organized evidence to quantify its degree of smoothing.

For each agent, the evidence is composed of: a source quote from the document, aspect detailing the assertion, a note on how the evidence bears on the claim, and strength rating.

blocks.en: Different cited documents can be relevant to different parts of a claim, so judging the claim against the raw documents forces the judge to compare evidence that is not directly comparable. If we look across the cited documents, however, the relevant information naturally clusters into topics that bear on the claim. For example, in Figure 2 , some documents discuss comparing the performance and efficiency of image tokens vs. diffusion approaches , while others discuss fit with LLM-style next-token scaling . We refer to these topics as aspects ( Kargupta et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 所引用的不同文件可能与索赔的不同部分有关,因此根据原始文件判断索赔迫使法官比较无法直接比较的证据。 但是,如果我们看一看所引用的文件,有关资料自然地将涉及索赔的专题分组。 例如,在图2中,一些文件讨论了将图像符号的性能和效率与传播方法进行比较的问题,而另一些文件则讨论了适合LLM-型的下位缩放问题。 我们将这些议题称为方面(Kargupta等人,2025年)。

blocks.en: To construct aspects, for each claim–document pair ( c i , d j ) ∈ C × D (c_{i},d_{j})\in C\times D we generate a set of document-specific aspect proposals, A i ​ j = Propose ⁡ ( c i , d j ) . A_{ij}=\operatorname{Propose}(c_{i},d_{j}). Each proposal identifies a dimension discussed in d j d_{j} that bears on c i c_{i} , and consists of a short name, a brief description, and a set of keywords. If d j d_{j} contains nothing relevant to c i c_{i} , then A i ​ j = ∅ A_{ij}=\varnothing (see Appendix B.4 for the prompt). Because proposals are generated independently for each document, different documents will often propose overlapping or near-duplicate aspects. For each claim, we therefore merge the proposals across documents into a single, deduplicated set of aspects, keeping track of which documents contributed to each one (see Appendix B.5 ).

blocks.zh: 4.2 定性意见

blocks.en: We find that query framing influences how the model writes its claims. As seen in Appendix G.1 and G.2 , there are certain categories of questions where smoothing is more pronounced: (1) Comparative questions: if the query is comparative in nature, for example, ‘In multimodal pretraining, the paradigms are based on image tokens and stable diffusion, which appears more promising and why?’ or ‘Which paradigm between RL and distillation appears more promising and why?’ , it can presuppose a choice from the agent where to motivate or justify a choice the agent drops important qualifications, (2) Topic overview questions: queries that require an overview of a topic, for example, ‘Describe the Sunflower conjecture, progress towards a solution, and related problems’ , the agent can assemble multiple results a single conclusion or just generalize from a single finding to the whole topic.
blocks.zh: 我们发现这种查询框架会影响模型如何写出它的说法。 如附录G.1和G.2所示,有些类别的问题比较明显: (1) 比较问题:如果查询的性质是比较的,例如`在多式联运预先训练中,范式是以图像符号和稳定的传播为基础的,这似乎更有希望,为什么? ' 或`RL和蒸馏之间的哪一个范式看来更有希望,为什么? ' ,那么,它可以预先假定从代理人那里作出一种选择,以促使代理人放弃重要资格或为其选择辩护;(2) 专题概览问题:需要对某一专题进行概述的询问,例如`描述向日葵猜想,走向解决办法的进展,以及相关问题 ' ,代理人可以汇集一个单一的结论,或只是将一个结论概括到整个专题。

blocks.en:
Table 2 shows three patterns that we observe across systems: (1) Unsupported composition : Agents combine individual fragments of evidence into a stronger conclusion. Although each component may be supported, the claim presents its unsupported composition as a conclusive statement. (2) Scope expansion : A claim takes an established result for a particular setup or experimental condition and removes certain boundaries, so that a the scope for an empirical observation expands into a general conclusion.
(3) Premature Closure : Claims often adopt conclusive language, using phrases like ‘strictly preserving,’ ‘the best approach,’ ‘definitively proves’ and ‘most optimal.’ .

(3) 提前结案:索赔往往采用结论性语言,使用诸如 " 严格保留 " 、 " 最佳办法 " 、 " 确切证明 " 和 " 最优化. " 等词语。

blocks.en: While human agreement validates the SmoothScore judge’s final scores, we separately check whether the evidence SmoothScore surfaces (Steps 2–4) is useful. We consider an independent measure, using gold rubrics provided by ResearcherBench created for judging the overall quality of the generated report. We take Luna and Sonnet 5 WebSearch reports on the benchmark, and perform an additional revision step with no web search under three context settings: (1) no additional context, (2) providing all cited documents, and (3) the collected SmoothScore evidence as context. We find that both context settings rise well above the no-context control ( + 0.4 +0.4 and + 1.1 +1.1 ), with the extracted evidence improving rubric scores for both agents (Luna + 4.4 +4.4 , Sonnet + 12.0 +12.0 , both p < .001 p<.001 ), matching or even exceeding revision with the full documents. The evidence achieves this with roughly one-fifth to one-tenth of the tokens of the full documents. While this does not test the quality of the evidence relative to the generated claims, it shows that the evidence captures information that matters to an external, expert-written evaluation independent of the judge’s scores.

blocks.en: 6 Lack of engagement with document content
blocks.zh: 6 缺乏对文件内容的参与

blocks.en: The systems we evaluate generate reports with citations from the documents they retrieve. However, the agent’s interaction with the cited material is hard to control. For Luna, the trace shows that the agent works almost entirely from search snippets truncated by the tool (median 585 characters), opening a cited page for only 19% of the documents it cites and in just 20 of 65 reports. Sonnet 5 engages even less, opening only 2% of the links it cites (Table 5 , Appendix F ). As agents rarely read the full documents, an agent may never see the qualifications and countervailing findings in the body of a source, which suggests that smoothing is partly shaped by what information the agent chooses to access.

blocks.en: 7 Related Work
blocks.zh: 7 相关工作

blocks.en: A standard recipe for verifying long-form text is to decompose it into smaller checkable units and score each against a knowledge source ( Min et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2024 ; Gunjal and Durrett, 2024 ) . These methods generally return a binary decision per claim, which is a good granularity for factual precision, but it does not work for synthesized claims that can have varying degrees of smoothing. ConflictScore ( Liu et al., 2026 ) is the closest to our setting, and it extends this atomic claim recipe in a direction close to ours. They mark a claim as supported, contradicted or irrelevant per document retrieved, and aggregate these into claim-level conflict measures. However, a claim can be labeled supported by every one of its cited documents and still smooth over information it omits. Our work instead follows Kargupta et al. (2025) in organizing evidence along aspects (e.g., viewpoint, strength, certainty), so that supporting and qualifying evidence on the feature of a claim can be considered against each other.
blocks.zh: 用于验证长式文本的标准配方是将其分解成较小的可核对单位,并分别对照知识源进行计分(Min等人,2023年;Chen等人,2024年;Gunjal和Durrett,2024年)。 这些方法一般还原每个索赔的二进制决定,对于事实精确性来说,这是一个很好的颗粒性,但对于能有不同程度平滑的合成索赔却不起作用. 冲突记分(Liu et al., 2026)是最接近于我们设定的,它将这种原子主张的秘方延伸至接近我们的方向. 它们将索赔标为证明、矛盾或不相干的每份所获取的文件,并将其合并为索赔一级的冲突措施。 然而,一项索赔可以由它所引述的每一份文件作为佐证,而且对于它省略的信息来说,仍然是顺畅的。 相反,我们的工作是遵循Kargupta等人(2025年)的做法,按方方面面组织证据(例如观点、力度、确定性),以便可以考虑关于索赔特征的佐证和合格证据。

blocks.en: In science communication, prior work measures certainty in how findings are stated ( Pei and Jurgens, 2021 ) and models how information changes as findings move from papers to news and social media ( Wright et al., 2022 ) . For LLM summaries of scientific text, Peters and Chin-Yee (2025) test ten widely used LLMs on about 4,900 summaries and find that most produce broader generalizations than the source texts, and that LLM summaries are nearly five times more likely than human-written ones to overgeneralize. In medicine, neural multi-document summaries of clinical trials are fluent but often factually inaccurate ( Wallace et al., 2021 ) , and LLM summaries of medical evidence can misstate the certainty of the evidence or overgeneralize by omitting attributes such as a disease subtype ( Tang et al., 2023 ) . These studies summarize a single document or a small set of abstracts. We extend the concern to long-form, multi-document research reports written by agents, and give a claim-level measure grounded in the documents a report cites.
blocks.zh: 在科学传播中,前期工作衡量了结论如何表述的确定性(Pei and Jurgens, 2021年),以及随着结论从论文转移到新闻和社交媒体的信息变化模式(Wright等人, 2022年). 对于科学文本的LLM摘要,Peters和Chin-Yee(2025年)在约4900个摘要上测试了十种被广泛使用的LLMs,发现大多数摘要产生比源文本更广泛的概括,LLM摘要比人文摘要更可能过度概括. 在医学方面,临床试验的神经多文件摘要很流利,但往往不准确(Wallace等人,2021年),医学证据的LLM摘要可能会通过省略疾病亚型等属性来错误表述证据的确定性或过度概括(Tang等人,2023年). 这些研究总结了一份文件或一套小摘要。 我们对由代理人撰写的长式多文件研究报告表示关切,并在报告所引用的文件中提出权利要求。

blocks.en: Agentic deep-research systems ( Du et al., 2026 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ; Sharma et al., 2025 ) pair rubric-based insight coverage with citation grounded factuality checks. Several works audit the reliability of these systems. DeepTRACE ( Narayanan Venkit et al., 2026 ) decomposes answers into statements and finds that deep-research agents remain one-sided on debate queries and include many statements unsupported by their listed sources. Onweller et al. (2026) find that citations that resolve and are topically relevant often still fail a factual check against the cited content. Zhu et al. (2026) show that a single misleading document can induce false conclusions in final reports. Rasheed et al. (2026) argue for claim-level auditability, including whether conflicts in the evidence are surfaced or suppressed. Across this literature, factuality is largely operationalized as citation validity: whether a claim is supported by some retrieved source. Our results show that this is not enough. Reports whose claims are individually supported can still present mixed or conditional evidence as a decisive conclusion, so assessing how faithfully the underlying evidence is presented requires the claim-level, evidence-calibrated analysis we propose.
blocks.zh: 代理深层研究系统(Du等人,2026年;徐等人,2026年;Huang等人,2026年;Li等人,2026年a;Sharma等人,2025年) 以引用依据事实检查为主的对面透视覆盖率。 一些工作对这些系统的可靠性进行审计。 DeepTRACE(Narayanan Venkit et al., 2026)将答案分解为声明,发现深层研究人员在辩论询问上仍持片面态度,并包含了许多没有其列表来源支持的声明. Onweller等人(2026年)发现,那些解决和与主题相关的引文往往仍未与所引用的内容进行事实核对。 Zhu等人(2026年)表明,一份单一的误导性文件可能在最后报告中引起错误的结论. Rasheed等人(2026年)主张索赔一级的可审计性,包括证据中的冲突是表面的还是压制的。 通过这些文献,事实性基本上可用作援引的有效性:索赔是否得到某些检索来源的支持。 我们的结果表明,这还不够。 其索赔得到个别支持的报告仍可提出混合或有条件的证据作为决定性结论,因此,要评估基本证据的提交是否忠实,就需要我们建议的索赔水平和证据校准分析。

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we studied the propensity of LLMs to smooth their conclusions when generating reports based on sources. They frequently generate oversimplified statements or conclusions that aren’t really backed up by the evidence cited. Our pipeline, SmoothScore , allows us to quantify this and establish its frequency across several state-of-the-art agents. Finally, we find that this models fail to read with their own cited documents, and suggest smoothing can improved by more thorough agents engaging wih their sources.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们研究了法学硕士在根据资料来源编写报告时是否倾向于顺利地作出结论。 他们经常产生过于简单的说法或结论, 我们的管道,光滑得分, 使我们能够量化这一点, 并确定它的频率 通过几个最先进的代理。 最后,我们发现这些模型没有用它们自己引用的文件来阅读,建议通过更彻底地接触它们的消息来源来改进平滑。

Prompt B.2: Supporting Evidence Extraction System Prompt: You extract from a single source DOCUMENT every distinct piece of information that SUPPORTS
a single CLAIM from a research report, or a specific part of it – makes what the claim
actually says more plausible or provides a direct instance/evidence for it. Extract ONLY supporting evidence. Ignore evidence against the claim entirely; another
process handles that. • POLARITY: support means supporting what the claim ACTUALLY ASSERTS. If the claim
asserts a limitation or a negative (e.g. “X is unreliable”, “X scales worse”,
“X does not generalize”), then evidence of X failing/underperforming is supporting,
and a result showing X working well is NOT supporting – skip it. • STATED CONCESSIONS ARE PART OF THE CLAIM: evidence confirming a limitation,
condition, or concession the claim itself states supports the claim as stated –
include it, with the concession named in the aspect field. An item is one distinct FINDING: a specific result, experiment, measurement, or stated
conclusion. Each item is an object: {"quote": "<the shortest verbatim excerpt that carries this finding>",
   "aspect": "<the specific assertion WITHIN the claim this finding bears
               on, quoted or near-verbatim from the claim>",
   "note": "<one sentence: how this finding bears on that assertion>",
   "strength": <1-5>}
strength = how directly and specifically this item bears on what the
claim asserts:
  1 = tangential  2 = weak/indirect  3 = moderate: relevant but partial
  or hedged
  4 = strong: direct, on-point  5 = decisive: exactly what the claim
  asserts (or a clear counterexample to it). Critical rules: • Judge ONLY against this one document. No outside knowledge, no other documents. • Read the WHOLE document; relevant evidence can sit in any section. • ONE item per finding. If the document states the same finding several ways
(abstract, body, conclusion), pick the single best quote for it – do not list
restatements or different facets of the same result as separate items. • Do NOT include items that only establish setting or applicability without an
outcome (e.g. “the experiments use a 1.5B model”). That is context, not evidence; if
it matters, mention it inside the note of a real item. • An empty list is a perfectly good answer – do NOT invent items. Merely being
about the same topic is NOT evidence; every item must actually move belief about the
claim in the direction you were asked for. • MECHANISM: only count evidence that matches what the claim specifically says
(e.g. if the claim says “distillation from a LARGER model”, a result using a
same-size or self-distilled model does not bear on that specific mechanism). The aspect
field must name the exact assertion addressed – if you cannot point to one, the item
does not belong. • Quotes must be copied verbatim from the document. Return only JSON: {"items": [ …]} User Prompt: Question (context only, not evidence): {{ Question }} Claim: {{ Claim }} Document: Title: {{ Document Title }} URL: {{ Document URL }} Content: {{ Full Document Text }} Extract every distinct piece of supporting evidence and return only the JSON object.

SKEPTICAL reader would weigh against a single CLAIM from a research report, and you TAG
each item by its relation to the claim AS STATED. Extract only this skeptical side; a
separate process handles supporting evidence. Read the claim carefully first: its actual assertions, its scope, its comparatives, and
every limitation, condition, or concession it ALREADY STATES or hedges over. TAGS: • "counter" : the finding cuts against what the claim ACTUALLY ASSERTS –
contradicts it, provides a counterexample, limits its scope beyond what it admits,
shows the asserted effect weaker or more conditional than asserted, or reports a null
or mixed result where the claim implies a clear one. POLARITY: if the claim asserts a
limitation or a negative (“X is unreliable”), a result showing X working WELL is a
counter, and evidence of X failing is NOT. A soft hedge does not concede everything:

evidence X merely SOMETIMES loses is not. • "concession-match" : the finding confirms, instantiates, or quantifies a
limitation, condition, or concession the claim ITSELF states or hedges over
(“capacity-sensitive”, “results vary”, “except in short contexts”). These do NOT
count against the claim – they are extracted so a later audit can check whether the
report states the substance behind its own hedges. • "rival-win" : a success of ANOTHER approach reported in that approach’s
own terms, where the claim does NOT rank over or exclude that approach. If the claim
DOES rank or exclude (“strongest”, “most practical”, “X remains ahead of Y”), a
rival’s success is a "counter" , not a "rival-win" . A carefully scoped claim often has NO counter items in a given document – an empty counter

rival-win items where they exist. • STRENGTH for "counter" = how much the finding should CONSTRAIN the claim

own stated scope; 4 = a hard limit or condition on the main assertion that the claim
does not state; 3 = a meaningful qualification; 2 = weak/indirect pressure;

blocks.en:
Prompt B.7: Evidence-Smoothing Judgment System Prompt: You are an evidence-smoothing judge. You assess how faithfully a claim compresses the evidence supplied to it — not whether the claim is well-written, complete, or true by outside standards. User Prompt: # Inputs Research question:
{{QUESTION}} Claim under evaluation:
{{CLAIM}} Evidence by aspect:
{{ASPECTS_AND_EVIDENCE}} Each evidence item may include: a source identifier, an exact quotation, a generated context note, and a retrieval-pass label (”support-pass candidate” / ”countervailing-pass candidate”). # What you’re measuring Evidence smoothing: the claim collapses material heterogeneity, uncertainty, conditionality, or disagreement in the evidence, producing a conclusion broader, more certain, more universal, or more decisive than the evidence proportionately warrants. Not in scope: coverage (the claim need not mention every finding), writing quality, or accuracy against knowledge outside the supplied evidence. # Ground rules for reading the evidence 1. **The supplied evidence is the entire universe.** No outside knowledge. 2. **Retrieval labels describe provenance, not verified stance.** Interpret each item’s actual content independently — a support-pass item can fail to support the claim; a countervailing-pass item can support, qualify, or be irrelevant to it. 3. **Item counts and pass labels are not evidence of consensus or its absence.** Never infer balance, or lack of it, from how many items landed in each pass. 4. **Context notes clarify; they don’t add evidence.** Ground judgments in the quotation. Preserve the claim’s actual scope, certainty, and role in answering the question. Do not weaken a strong assertion into a vague statement of usefulness, or strengthen a qualified claim into an unconditional guarantee. 5. **Weigh by relevance, directness, applicability, and any quality signal stated in the text — not by quote count.** Restatements of the same finding are one data point, not several. 6. **The claim’s own logical force sets what can defeat it:**
- ”X can work” — isolated failures of X don’t count against it.
- ”X always / necessarily works” — one sound counterexample is decisive.
- ”X generally works / dominates” — isolated counterexamples aren’t enough; the evidence must speak to prevalence or the overall comparison.
- ”X is promising” — a rival promising method doesn’t refute it.
- ”X is comparatively best” — comparable alternatives are directly relevant.
- A claim need not preempt exceptions its own wording already allows. 7. **Absence of support ≠ \neq contradiction**, but an unsupported specific assertion is still unwarranted — weight this by whether it’s peripheral or central to the takeaway. 8. **For multi-part claims, weight problems by their effect on the overall takeaway.** Don’t average proposition-level defects or default to the score triggered by the single worst one. # Procedure Work through these in order. Your response’s structure follows this order (see Output). 1. **Claim’s contribution.** What is the claim doing relative to the question — explaining a possibility, asserting a general pattern, reporting a result, making a recommendation? This determines what kind of evidence can defeat it. 2. **Substantive takeaway.** State the scope, certainty, comparison, and causal content the claim actually asserts, independent of phrasing. Don’t pre-weaken an overstated claim before judging it. 3. **Positive evidential case.** What do the relevant findings, taken together, justify? Include reasonable inferences across findings. Flag anything the claim asserts that the evidence doesn’t actually reach (a specific mechanism, magnitude, or comparison it never establishes), even if the surrounding evidence is generally favorable. 4. **Objections.** For each apparent counterpoint: does it address the same assertion, in the applicable setting? Distinguish a consequential restriction from a compatible failure, a different mechanism, or an unrelated limitation. Treat a finding as an outlier only when the evidence itself gives a basis for that, not because it’s outnumbered or inconvenient. 5. **Net resolution.** Combine 3 and 4. Does the claim survive as stated, survive with a limitation attached, or require a substantially different conclusion? 6. Score via the minimum-repair test below. # Minimum-repair test Determine the score by identifying the minimum semantic revision needed to make the claim faithful to the supplied evidence. Work through these levels in order and stop at the first one that fits: - None: the claim can remain as written. Omitted material would only elaborate or add background. A further caveat could be written, but none is needed for fidelity. - Append: a caveat or exception should be added for the claim to represent the evidence faithfully, but the original claim otherwise remains — its central scope, certainty, comparison, and conclusion stay substantially unchanged. - Revise: the claim’s central direction survives, but a material predicate, quantifier, scope, comparison, causal attribution, or confidence level must be changed. A reader who accepted the original would draw a materially different conclusion from the repaired version. - Recast: the overall conclusion must be substantially narrowed, rebalanced, or made explicitly mixed. A recognizable part of the original takeaway survives, but not the conclusion as presented. - Replace: the central takeaway cannot be preserved. A faithful account requires a materially different conclusion; adding qualifications or rebalancing is insufficient. Do not select Append merely because an additional caveat could be written — select it only when a caveat is genuinely needed for faithful representation. Do not select Revise for a hedge the claim’s own wording already implies (e.g. adding ”generally” to a claim that elsewhere says ”typically”) — that is an Append. # Scoring rubric Each repair level corresponds to exactly one score: None → \rightarrow 1 (Reasonable compression). The claim preserves important conditions and fairly represents relevant counterevidence. Omitted details do not meaningfully change the takeaway. Append → \rightarrow 2 (Minor nuance lost). Some conditions, limitations, or exceptions are omitted, but including them would leave the takeaway largely unchanged. Revise → \rightarrow 3 (Important qualification missing). An important condition, limitation, or exception is omitted, making the claim broader or more certain than warranted. The central takeaway remains defensible with that qualification. Recast → \rightarrow 4 (Major distortion). Substantial counterevidence or a decisive limitation is omitted or understated. The claim presents a clear conclusion where the evidence requires substantial narrowing, rebalancing, or a mixed conclusion. Replace → \rightarrow 5 (Fundamentally misleading). The claim fundamentally misrepresents what the evidence warrants — for example, by omitting both crucial conditions and strong counterevidence. The central takeaway needs replacing; adding qualifications alone cannot make it faithful. Direct contradiction is not required. # Deciding the score Decide from the state of the evidence around the central takeaway, then confirm against the rubric above. Only material bearing on the central takeaway counts here. Material that qualifies a subsidiary assertion — an example, a mechanism, a side-condition, an intensifier — does not move the score unless correcting it changes the takeaway itself. The claim’s hedges are part of its wording. “Likely”, “often”, “when X”, “reducing” set what has to be shown. Evidence that the claim is not uniformly or always true does not bear against a claim that never asserted universality. - Nothing in the evidence bears against the takeaway, or what does is already allowed by the claim’s own wording → \rightarrow 1 - What bears against it is narrower in scope, less direct, or less consistent than what supports it — the takeaway holds with surety → \rightarrow 2 - What bears against it is as direct and as broad as what supports it — the takeaway is arguably correct but contested → \rightarrow 3 - What bears against it outweighs the support, or the two together leave the central question genuinely two-sided — a faithful account is mixed → \rightarrow 4 - The evidence never establishes the takeaway, or establishes something materially different → \rightarrow 5 The repair labels — none, append, revise, recast, replace — describe the consequence of the score and are reported for auditing. They are not the test. Before assigning a score, identify a material qualification required by the evidence that is not already conveyed by the claim’s wording or context. # Output Return a single JSON object with exactly these fields, in this order. No text before or after the JSON. {
  "claim_role": "<one sentence: what kind of claim this is
  (possibility / general pattern / result / recommendation),
  and what that implies for what can defeat it>",

  "takeaway": "<the claim’s actual scope, certainty, comparison,
  and causal content, stated plainly>",

  "positive_case": "<what the relevant evidence, taken together,
  establishes, and, if applicable, what the claim asserts beyond
  what the evidence actually reaches>",

  "objections": "<what the countervailing or qualifying evidence
  actually changes, if anything; use ’none material’ if nothing
  meaningfully bears on the claim as scoped>",

  "net_resolution": "<does the claim survive as-is, survive with
  a limitation, or need substantial revision, and why, in 1-2
  sentences>",

  "repair": "none | append | revise | recast | replace",

  "score": 1
} Constraints:
- ”repair” and ”score” must correspond exactly: none=1, append=2, revise=3, recast=4, replace=5.
- ”score” must be an integer, not a string.
- Every field is required. Do not add extra fields.
- Output must be valid JSON — no markdown code fences, no trailing commas, no comments.

- “X能起作用”——X的孤立失败不能算作是失败。
- “X总是/必然有效”——一个声音反例是决定性的。
- “X一般可行/占主导地位”——孤立的反例是不够的;证据必须说明普遍性或总体比较。

blocks.en:
Luna and Sol use the OpenAI Responses API web search tool, whose calls are recorded as search, page-open, or find-in-page actions ( OpenAI, 2026 ) . We count a cited link as opened if the returned search results contain that page’s opened content, marked by a Source: open(…) header. These markers capture every page-open and find-in-page action, as well as opens returned inside other calls’ results, so counting the actions alone would miss about three quarters of them. Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5 run with Anthropic’s web search and web fetch tools. Search results return page content in encrypted form, so we cannot observe what the model sees from search alone, while web fetch retrieves a page’s full text ( Anthropic, 2026b ; Anthropic, 2026a ) . We therefore count a cited link as opened if the system successfully fetched it. As search results are encrypted, this measures full-page retrieval only; we cannot
observe how much page content the model receives from search. For DR Tulu, we count calls to its browsing tool ( Shao et al., 2026 ) . All five systems cite mostly from search results rather than pages they open. Luna and Sol open 9–19% and 16–30% of the links they cite (45 of Luna’s 65 ResearcherBench reports open no cited page), Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5 fetch 1.1–3.5% and 0.2–2.3%, and DR Tulu calls its browsing tool only 5 times across all datasets.

Luna and Sol使用OpenAI Response API网络搜索工具,其通话被记录为搜索,页面打开,或查找页面动作(OpenAI, 2026 ) . 如果返回的搜索结果包含该页打开的内容, 我们算上一个引用的链接是打开的 , 并用源: 打开(...) 页眉来标记 。 这些标记记录了每一个打开页面和查找页面的动作,以及打开在其他呼叫结果中返回的动作,因此仅仅计算这些动作就会错过大约四分之三的动作. Sonnet 5和Opus 5.5使用Anthropic的网络搜索和网络获取工具运行。 搜索结果以加密的形式返回页面内容,因此我们无法单独观察模型从搜索中看到的,而网页获取检索到一个页面的全文(Anthropic, 2026b;Anthropic, 2026a). 因此,如果系统成功获取,我们算上一个引用的链接是打开的。 由于搜索结果是加密的,因此只能测量全页检索;我们不能
观察该模型从搜索中获得的页面内容。 就Tulu博士而言,我们数到它的浏览工具(Shao等人,2026年)。 所有五个系统都主要引用搜索结果而不是打开的网页。 Luna and Sol打开了9–19 % 和 16–30 % 的链接(Luna的65位研究员Bench报告没有打开引用页),Sonnet 5和Opus 5.5获取1.1–3.5 % 和 0.2–2.3 % , DR Tulu称其浏览工具在所有数据集中只有5次。

blocks.en: QUEST’s visit tool does not return the raw page content to the agent: a separate model (GPT-5-mini) reads the page and returns an extract conditioned on a goal QUEST states for the visit, consisting of selected evidence and a short summary ( Xie et al., 2026 ) . We count a cited link as opened if QUEST issued a visit to it. Its high open rate therefore does not mean QUEST reads what it cites: the agent sees only extracts filtered toward what it was looking for, which is consistent with its high smoothing despite frequent visits.
blocks.zh: QUST的访问工具不会将原始的页面内容还给代理商:一个单独的模型(GPT-5-mini)读取页面,并返回一个以QUST目标状态为访问条件的摘录,包括选定的证据和一份简短摘要(Xie等人,2026年). 我们把一个引用的链接算作是开放的,如果 " 请求 " 组织对它进行了访问。 因此,其高开放率并不意味着 " 请求 " 阅读它所引述的内容:代理人只看到过滤到它所寻求的东西的提取物,这与它尽管经常访问却保持高平滑是一致的。

blocks.en: The Deep Research API returns only the final report and its citation links, with no browsing or tool steps, so engagement cannot be measured.
blocks.zh: Deep Research API只返回最终报告及其引用链接,没有浏览或工具步骤,因此不能衡量参与.
